lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: choosing the appropriate law for a given triangle
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: choosing the appropriate law for a given triangle

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: A triangle problem gives two angles and any side (AAS or ASA). Which law should be used first?
choices: the law of sines, with a check for the ambiguous case

items.prompt: In a triangle, sides a = 12 and b = 12 enclose an angle C = 120°. Find c², the square of the third side.
In a triangle, angle A = 31°, angle B = 81°, and side a = 16 (opposite A). Find side b to two decimal places.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A triangle has sides a = 4 and b = 12 enclosing an angle of 90°. Find its area exactly.
A triangle problem gives two sides and the angle between them (SAS). Which law should be used first?
choices: the law of sines, with a check for the ambiguous case

items.prompt: In a triangle, sides a = 9 and b = 5 enclose an angle C = 60°. Find c², the square of the third side.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: In a triangle, angle A = 58°, angle B = 79°, and side a = 9 (opposite A). Find side b to two decimal places.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A triangle has sides a = 10 and b = 15 enclosing an angle of 150°. Find its area exactly.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
